import hashlib, os, sys
ROOT = '/tmp/greenfield-34-final-empty-claude-4q_c5wya'
def _check(rel):
    parts = rel.split('/')
    if rel.startswith('/') or any(p in ('', '.', '..') for p in parts):
        sys.exit('unsafe path: ' + rel)
    cur = ROOT
    for p in parts[:-1]:
        cur = os.path.join(cur, p)
        if os.path.islink(cur) or not os.path.isdir(cur):
            sys.exit('unapproved or unsafe parent: ' + cur)
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, rel)
    if os.path.islink(path):
        sys.exit('symlink target refused: ' + rel)
    return path
def mkdir(rel):
    os.mkdir(_check(rel), 0o755)
    print('WRITE: ' + rel + '/')
def create(rel, text):
    fd = os.open(_check(rel), os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o644)
    with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write(text)
    print('WRITE: ' + rel)
def _guard(rel, before):
    path = _check(rel)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        sys.exit('missing edit target: ' + rel)
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
    actual = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    if actual != before:
        sys.exit('before-hash mismatch for ' + rel + ': ' + actual)
    return path, data
def replace(rel, before, text):
    path, _ = _guard(rel, before)
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_TRUNC | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write(text)
    print('WRITE: ' + rel)
def append(rel, before, extra):
    path, data = _guard(rel, before)
    fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write(extra)

## Product

greenfield-proof: a small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus a CLI for developers. `greet(name?: string)` returns `Hello, <name>!`, defaults to `world`, and rejects blank names with a `TypeError`. Developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI.

## Platforms

## Constraints

- Any network, service, or authentication behaviour.

Non-Blade. No brand values exist and none are invented.

create('docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md', '''# ADR 0001: Technology stack

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-09-05

## Context

greenfield-proof is a small TypeScript reusable greeting API plus a CLI for developers, managed with npm, targeting Node 22+ on Linux, private and UNLICENSED with no publishing. It needs a bundler for `dist/` exports and a `bin`, a type check, and a test runner with minimal dependencies. No framework runtime, external service, authentication, mobile target, deployment, or product remote applies. The greeting API is an in-process library export, not a network API, so the Backend matrix was not presented.

## Options

### Library/CLI
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: tsup + node:test — selected for a small TypeScript package that values minimal test dependencies; tsup (https://tsup.egoist.dev/, MIT, Allowed anywhere) builds `src/index.ts` and `src/cli.ts` to ESM with declarations, and node:test (https://nodejs.org/api/test.html) runs behaviour tests without a test dependency.

Generator: the library-cli archetype's create-vite (https://vite.dev/guide/, MIT, Allowed anywhere), version 8.3.0 from the local npx cache and byte-verified against the published archive, template `vanilla-ts`, run into the repository root. Its web demo files were removed and `vite` was dropped from devDependencies because the package has no browser surface.

## Consequences

- Positive: one build tool, no test framework dependency, ESM-only output published through `exports`, `bin`, and `files`.
- Positive: source and tests run unbuilt under Node 22 type stripping, so `node --test` does not depend on `dist/`.
- Negative: no linter or formatter is installed; style is enforced only by the strict compiler flags recorded in `docs/CODE-STYLE.md`.
- Negative: `tsx` and `zod` are development dependencies solely for the roadmap emit tooling.

## Revisit when

A second output format, a browser target, or a test need beyond node:test assertions appears, or the package is scheduled for publishing.
''')

## Status

Accepted

## Date

2026-09-05

## Context

greenfield-proof is a library plus a command-line adapter with no user interface: its only surfaces are exported functions and text on stdout and stderr. It is non-Blade, so no sibling design handoff applies, and no brand values exist. Platforms: Node 22+ on Linux; mobile: none.

## Options
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shadcn/ui | Source-owned accessible components | Consumer maintains copied components | Tailored product UI needs full control | Components and registry items compose locally | https://ui.shadcn.com/docs |
| Radix Themes | Cohesive accessible component theme | Stronger visual conventions | Fast consistent UI matters more than source ownership | Theme primitives compose across screens | @radix-ui/themes |
| MUI | Broad mature component suite | Larger runtime and opinionated styling | Enterprise UI needs extensive ready-made widgets | Shared theme and component packages | @mui/material |

## Ruling

2026-09-05: No design system — the package has no UI surface, so none of the options applies; the selected registry is none, and no tokens, themes, fonts, palette, or spacing values are invented. The UX canon records the CLI text contract instead.

For Blade, store pointers only; tokens are owned by zeroh-design. Not applicable: this repository is non-Blade.

## Consequences

- Positive: no UI dependency, token home, or registry to maintain.
- Negative: if a UI surface is ever added, a design-system decision must be made from these options before any component is written.

## Revisit when

Any web, mobile, or terminal UI component beyond plain text output is proposed, or Blade branding is requested.

## Lint

`none` (no linter is installed or configured; the archetype generator adds none and none was proposed)

## Format

`none` (no formatter is installed or configured; source follows the generated style: two-space indentation, single quotes, no semicolons, trailing commas in multi-line literals)

create('docs/ux-canon.md', '''# UX canon

## Visual language

None. greenfield-proof has no graphical surface; its only user-facing output is plain UTF-8 text on stdout and stderr. No fonts, palette, or spacing values exist and none are invented.

## Component vocabulary

- Greeting line: `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline on stdout.
- Usage text: starts with `Usage: greenfield-proof [name] [--help]` and lists the options.
- Error line: one human-readable sentence followed by the usage text on stderr.

## Interaction rules

- `greenfield-proof` with no argument prints the default greeting and exits 0.
- `greenfield-proof <name>` prints the greeting for that name and exits 0.
- `--help` or `-h` prints the usage text on stdout and exits 0.
- An unknown option, more than one positional argument, or a blank name prints an error line plus the usage text on stderr and exits 1.
- An unknown option always exits 1, even when `--help` or `-h` is also present in any position; help never masks an invalid invocation.
- Output is deterministic and never colored, interactive, or dependent on the terminal.

## Binding design system

None. Non-Blade with no UI surface; `designHomes.ux.bindingDesignSystem` is intentionally unset (ADR 0002).
''')
